Local business

Guessing cost more than the flour

By our sample correspondent

For years, the owner decided how much to bake the way many small shops do: by looking at the weather and trusting a hunch.

On rainy days the shelves stayed full. On sunny ones, the bread was gone by ten and customers walked away.

Think of it as packing for a trip without checking the forecast: you carry too much, or you get wet. Either way, you pay for it.

Opinion

Should a shop trust a forecast?

In favor

It catches what we forget

Holidays, paydays, the first cold week: patterns nobody can keep in their head.

Against

It can't see a street fair

A forecast only knows the past. The owner still has the final say every morning.
